"'''Rockstar'''" (stylized in [[all lowercase]]) is a song by American musician [[Post Malone]] featuring British-American rapper [[21 Savage]]. It was released on September 15, 2017, by [[Republic Records]] as the [[lead single]] from Malone's second studio album ''[[Beerbongs & Bentleys]]'' (2018). The song was written alongside Carl Rosen, [[Joey Badass|Joey Bada$$]], and producers [[Louis Bell]] and Tank God.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://genius.com/artists/Tank-producer|title=Genius: artists|publisher=Genius|access-date=September 26, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.xxlmag.com/news/2017/09/post-malone-21-savage-rockstar/|title=Post Malone 21 Savage Rockstar|work=[[XXL (magazine)|XXL]]|date=15 September 2017 |access-date=September 26, 2017}}</ref><ref name=AllMusic>{{cite web|title=Post Malone: Rockstar – Overview|url=https://www.allmusic.com/album/rockstar-mw0003108813|website=[[AllMusic]]|publisher=RhythmOne|access-date=January 5, 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180105004631/https://www.allmusic.com/album/rockstar-mw0003108813|archive-date=January 5, 2018}}</ref><ref name="BMISongwriters">{{cite web|publisher=[[Broadcast Music, Inc.]]|url=http://repertoire.bmi.com/Catalog.aspx?detail=artistid&page=1&fromrow=1&torow=25&keyid=792452&subid=0|title=Repertoire Search|access-date=January 26, 2018|archive-date=January 25, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180125195345/http://repertoire.bmi.com/Catalog.aspx?detail=artistid&page=1&fromrow=1&torow=25&keyid=792452&subid=0|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The track received mixed reviews from music critics, and became the artists' most successful hit single to date, reaching number one on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], and reaching the top spot in several other countries, including Australia, Canada, Greece, Portugal, Romania, Ireland, New Zealand, Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark and the United Kingdom. It became both Post Malone and 21 Savage's first number-one single in all the countries mentioned. The song was nominated for [[Grammy Award for Record of the Year|Record of the Year]] and [[Grammy Award for Best Rap/Sung Performance|Best Rap/Sung Performance]] at the [[61st Annual Grammy Awards]].

Post Malone posted a snippet of himself playing the track in the studio via [[Twitter]] on December 24, 2016.{{Citation needed|date=January 2024}}

"Rockstar" (stylized in all lowercase) is a song by American musician Post Malone featuring British-American rapper 21 Savage. It was released on September 15, 2017, by Republic Records as the lead single from Malone's second studio album Beerbongs & Bentleys (2018). The song was written alongside Carl Rosen, Joey Bada$$, and producers Louis Bell and Tank God.

The track received mixed reviews from music critics, and became the artists' most successful hit single to date, reaching number one on the US Billboard Hot 100, and reaching the top spot in several other countries, including Australia, Canada, Greece, Portugal, Romania, Ireland, New Zealand, Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark and the United Kingdom. It became both Post Malone and 21 Savage's first number-one single in all the countries mentioned. The song was nominated for Record of the Year and Best Rap/Sung Performance at the 61st Annual Grammy Awards.

Post Malone posted a snippet of himself playing the track in the studio via Twitter on December 24, 2016.{{Citation needed|date=January 2024}}

sections.heading: Music videos
sections.wikitext:
The now-private unofficial YouTube video for the track's audio, released by [[Republic Records]], is a three-minute-and-38-second loop of solely the song's chorus.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Gaca|first1=Anna|title=Post Malone's "rockstar" Probably Went to No. 1 Thanks to This Ridiculous Video|url=https://www.spin.com/2017/10/post-malone-rockstar-number-1-youtube-chorus-video/|website=Spin|access-date=22 November 2017|date=17 October 2017}}</ref> Therefore, the song was able to receive equivalent downloads without featuring the entirety of the song, which some attributed to its number-one spot on the Hot 100.<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Trammell|first1=Matthew|title=Post Malone's "Rockstar" and YouTube's Value Gap|url=https://www.newyorker.com/culture/culture-desk/post-malones-rockstar-and-youtubes-value-gap|magazine=The New Yorker|access-date=22 November 2017|date=18 October 2017}}</ref> Some called it a "clever marketing scheme", while others believed it was a trick or a loophole.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Tanzer|first1=Myles|title=How a weird YouTube hack helped Post Malone's "rockstar" get to No. 1 on the Billboard charts|url=http://www.thefader.com/2017/10/17/post-malone-youtube-rockstar-chorus-loop|website=The Fader|date=3 August 2017 |access-date=22 November 2017}}</ref>

The official music video, directed by [[Emil Nava]], was released on Post Malone's [[Vevo]] YouTube channel on November 21, 2017.<ref name=RockstarYouTube>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UceaB4D0jpo|title=Post Malone – rockstar ft. 21 Savage|date=21 November 2017 |publisher=YouTube|access-date=November 21, 2017}}</ref> The video features Post Malone in a room fighting against a gang of men with samurai swords, and ends with Post Malone and 21 Savage covered in blood.<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Brandle|first1=Lars|title=Post Malone's New 'Rockstar' Music Video is Ultraviolent: Watch|url=https://www.billboard.com/articles/news/8046244/post-malone-rockstar-music-video-ultraviolent|magazine=Billboard|access-date=23 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Orcutt|first1=KC|title=Post Malone and 21 Savage Drop Bloody ''Rockstar'' Video - XXL|url=http://www.xxlmag.com/news/2017/11/post-malone-21-savage-rockstar-video/|website=XXL Mag|date=22 November 2017 |access-date=23 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Renshaw|first1=David|title=Post Malone and 21 Savage star in the blood-soaked "rockstar" video|url=https://www.thefader.com/2017/11/22/post-malone-and-21-savage-star-in-the-blood-soaked-rockstar-video|website=The FADER|access-date=23 November 2017|language=en}}</ref> ''[[Pitchfork (website)|Pitchfork]]'' noted that the video references the Japanese action film ''[[Lady Snowblood (film)|Lady Snowblood]]''.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Minsker|first1=Evan|title=Post Malone and 21 Savage Drop Ultra-Bloody New "rockstar" Video: Watch|url=https://pitchfork.com/news/post-malone-and-21-savage-get-super-bloody-in-new-rockstar-video-watch/|website=Pitchfork|date=22 November 2017 |access-date=23 November 2017|language=en}}</ref> On June 23, 2022, after nearly five years on YouTube, the video hit one billion views.
sections.text:
The now-private unofficial YouTube video for the track's audio, released by Republic Records, is a three-minute-and-38-second loop of solely the song's chorus. Therefore, the song was able to receive equivalent downloads without featuring the entirety of the song, which some attributed to its number-one spot on the Hot 100. Some called it a "clever marketing scheme", while others believed it was a trick or a loophole.

The official music video, directed by Emil Nava, was released on Post Malone's Vevo YouTube channel on November 21, 2017. The video features Post Malone in a room fighting against a gang of men with samurai swords, and ends with Post Malone and 21 Savage covered in blood. Pitchfork noted that the video references the Japanese action film Lady Snowblood. On June 23, 2022, after nearly five years on YouTube, the video hit one billion views.

sections.heading: Commercial performance
sections.wikitext:
The song reached number one on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]], becoming Post Malone and 21 Savage's first number-one song.<ref name="Number One">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/post-malone-21-savage-rockstar-hot-100-no-1/|title=Post Malone & 21 Savage's 'Rockstar' Tops Hot 100|magazine=Billboard|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=October 16, 2017|access-date=October 17, 2017}}</ref> It debuted at number two behind [[Cardi B]]'s "[[Bodak Yellow]]",<ref name="Billboard debut">{{cite web|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/cardi-b-no-1-hot-100-post-malone-portugal-the-man/|title=Cardi B 'Moves' to No. 1 on Billboard Hot 100 With 'Bodak Yellow,' Post Malone Debuts at No. 2 With 'Rockstar'|magazine=Billboard|last=Trust|first=Gary|date=September 25, 2017|access-date=September 26, 2017}}</ref> breaking the single week streaming record on Apple Music with over 25 million streams,<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.xxlmag.com/news/2017/09/post-malone-rockstar-apple-music-streaming-record/|title=Post Malone Rockstar Apple Music Record|magazine=XXL|access-date=September 26, 2017}}</ref> becoming Post Malone's third top 20 hit, following his debut single, "[[White Iverson]]" and his second top 10 hit after "[[Congratulations (Post Malone song)|Congratulations]]". It stayed behind "[[Bodak Yellow]]" for three consecutive weeks before reaching the top spot in its fourth week.<ref name="Number One"/> "Rockstar" topped the Hot 100 for eight weeks, the longest run at number one for a hip-hop song in 2017. After its eighth week at number one, it was knocked off by "[[Perfect (Ed Sheeran song)|Perfect]]" by [[Ed Sheeran]] and [[Beyoncé]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/ed-sheeran-beyonce-perfect-billboard-hot-100-number-one/|title=Ed Sheeran & Beyonce's 'Perfect' Tops Billboard Hot 100|magazine=Billboard|first=Gary|last=Trust|date=December 11, 2017|access-date=December 11, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.billboard.com/pro/post-malone-21-savage-camila-cabello-havana-hot-100/|title=Post Malone & 21 Savage No. 1 on Billboard Hot 100 for Fourth Week, Camila Cabello's 'Havana' Surges to No. 2|magazine=Billboard|first=Gary|last=Trust|date=November 6, 2017|access-date=November 7, 2017}}</ref> The single has sold over 10,000,000 copies, being certified Diamond in the US.

In New Zealand, it debuted at number four, then moved to the top spot the following week, staying at the summit for eight weeks.

In Australia, it topped the [[ARIA Charts|ARIA Singles Chart]] for seven weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ariacharts.com.au/news/2017/seven-weeks-at-the-top-for-post-malone-s-rockstar|title=Seven weeks at the top for Post Malone's Rockstar|publisher=[[Australian Recording Industry Association]]|date=November 11, 2017|access-date=November 11, 2017}}</ref>

In 21 Savage's native United Kingdom, "Rockstar" debuted at number five on the [[UK Singles Chart]] on September 22, 2017. The following week, it rose three places to number two, behind [[Sam Smith (singer)|Sam Smith]]'s "[[Too Good at Goodbyes]]",<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.officialcharts.com/chart-news/post-malones-rockstar-is-narrowly-denied-a-uk-number-1-by-sam-smith__20595/|title=Post Malone narrowly denied UK Number 1 single by Sam Smith|publisher=[[Official Charts Company]]|access-date=November 2, 2017}}</ref> before reaching the top of the chart on October 6, 2017.

In September 2020, "Rockstar" became the second song ever, after Ed Sheeran's "[[Shape of You]]", to surpass [[List of most-streamed songs on Spotify|two billion streams]] on the audio platform [[Spotify]].
sections.text:
The song reached number one on the US Billboard Hot 100, becoming Post Malone and 21 Savage's first number-one song. It debuted at number two behind Cardi B's "Bodak Yellow", breaking the single week streaming record on Apple Music with over 25 million streams, becoming Post Malone's third top 20 hit, following his debut single, "White Iverson" and his second top 10 hit after "Congratulations". It stayed behind "Bodak Yellow" for three consecutive weeks before reaching the top spot in its fourth week. "Rockstar" topped the Hot 100 for eight weeks, the longest run at number one for a hip-hop song in 2017. After its eighth week at number one, it was knocked off by "Perfect" by Ed Sheeran and Beyoncé. The single has sold over 10,000,000 copies, being certified Diamond in the US.

In New Zealand, it debuted at number four, then moved to the top spot the following week, staying at the summit for eight weeks.

In Australia, it topped the ARIA Singles Chart for seven weeks.

In 21 Savage's native United Kingdom, "Rockstar" debuted at number five on the UK Singles Chart on September 22, 2017. The following week, it rose three places to number two, behind Sam Smith's "Too Good at Goodbyes", before reaching the top of the chart on October 6, 2017.

In September 2020, "Rockstar" became the second song ever, after Ed Sheeran's "Shape of You", to surpass two billion streams on the audio platform Spotify.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: "Rockstar" received mixed reviews from music critics. ''[[Spin (magazine)|Spin.com]]'' reviewed the song's unofficial video by stating: "The chorus loop may be a weirdly hypnotic, post-Vine marketing gimmick, but it seems like it worked. "rockstar" is both Post Malone's and 21 Savage's first-ever No. 1 single, meaning this probably won't be the last time an artist attempts to boost a track by distilling its catchiest section into a standalone product. Maybe, in the future, we'll all listen to seconds-long hooks on endless extended loops".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.spin.com/2017/10/post-malone-rockstar-number-1-youtube-chorus-video/|title=Post Malone's "rockstar" Probably Went to No. 1 Thanks to This Ridiculous Video|work=Spin|date=October 17, 2017|access-date=December 3, 2017}}</ref> ''Spin'' and ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' both named the song one of the worst of 2017.<ref>{{cite web|first=SPIN|last=Staff|url=https://www.spin.com/2018/01/the-worst-songs-of-2017/|title=The Worst Songs We Heard in 2017|work=SPIN|date=2 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|first=Time|last=Staff|url=https://time.com/5048308/top-10-worst-songs-2017/|title=Top 10 Worst Songs 2017: Katy Perry, Ed Sheeran|magazine=Time|date=22 December 2017|access-date=17 November 2024|archive-date=5 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190205150737/http://time.com/5048308/top-10-worst-songs-2017/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

"rockstar" is both Post Malone's and 21 Savage's first-ever No. 1 single, meaning this probably won't be the last time an artist attempts to boost a track by distilling its catchiest section into a standalone product. Maybe, in the future, we'll all listen to seconds-long hooks on endless extended loops". Spin and Time both named the song one of the worst of 2017.

sections.heading: Remixes
sections.wikitext: On November 29, 2017, an unofficial [[Crankdat]] remix of the song was released on the Trap Nation channel on YouTube. On December 13, 2017, a Latin remix of the song featuring Dominican-Puerto Rican [[reggaeton]] artists [[Nicky Jam]] and [[Ozuna (singer)|Ozuna]] was released.<ref>{{cite magazine|last1=Fernandez|first1=Suzette|title=Post Malone Drops 'Rockstar' Latin Remix Featuring Nicky Jam & Ozuna: Listen|url=https://www.billboard.com/music/latin/post-malone-rockstar-latin-remix-nicky-jam-ozuna-listen-8070532/|magazine=Billboard|access-date=December 14, 2017}}</ref> Another remix was released on December 22, 2017, featuring new verses from rappers [[Jadakiss]] and Nino Man.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/78535-jadakiss-and-nino-man-deliver-remix-of-post-malones-rockstar-new-song|title=Jadakiss & Nino Man Deliver Remix Of Post Malone's "Rockstar"|work=HotNewHipHop|access-date=March 10, 2018}}</ref> On December 25, 2017, [[Lil Wayne]] released his remix of the song, titled "5 Star" featuring [[Nicki Minaj]], as a single from his mixtape ''[[Dedication 6]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/78887-lil-wayne-and-nicki-minaj-team-up-for-rockstar-freestyle-5-star-new-song|title=Lil Wayne & Nicki Minaj Team Up For "Rockstar" Freestyle "5 Star"|work=HotNewHipHop|access-date=March 10, 2018}}</ref> On January 23, 2018, American rapper [[Fetty Wap]] released his remix of the song.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.hotnewhiphop.com/80454-fetty-wap-tackles-post-malones-rockstar-for-the-g-mix-new-song|title=Fetty Wap Tackles Post Malone's "Rockstar" For The G-Mix|work=HotNewHipHop|access-date=March 10, 2018}}</ref>
sections.text: On November 29, 2017, an unofficial Crankdat remix of the song was released on the Trap Nation channel on YouTube. On December 13, 2017, a Latin remix of the song featuring Dominican-Puerto Rican reggaeton artists Nicky Jam and Ozuna was released. Another remix was released on December 22, 2017, featuring new verses from rappers Jadakiss and Nino Man. On December 25, 2017, Lil Wayne released his remix of the song, titled "5 Star" featuring Nicki Minaj, as a single from his mixtape Dedication 6. On January 23, 2018, American rapper Fetty Wap released his remix of the song.
